findings.title: Argon2id Memory Cost Below OWASP Recommendation
findings.summary: Argon2id memoryCost is 64 MB (65536 KiB) while OWASP recommends minimum 19456 KiB for baseline and 65536 KiB recommended. The parallelism of 1 further reduces GPU memory pressure for offline attackers.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker obtains a dump of the users collection and runs offline brute-force attacks. With memoryCost=64MB and parallelism=1, modern GPU clusters can test significantly more candidates per second than with OWASP-recommended parallelism=4.
findings.impact: Offline cracking speed is higher than necessary. Lower work factor for offline brute-force attacks against leaked password databases.
findings.rootCause: Parameters were set to match a reference example rather than OWASP Argon2id baseline.
findings.remediation: Increase parallelism to 4 (OWASP recommendation) while keeping memoryCost at 64 MB: memoryCost: 65536, timeCost: 3, parallelism: 4.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Argon2id parameters match or exceed OWASP recommended baseline. Existing passwords continue to verify (backward compatible).
requiredTests: Verify hashPassword() produces hash with p=4
Verify verifyPassword() succeeds against old p=1 hashes
Measure hash time on deployment platform (100-500ms)

findings.title: Argon2id Parallelism Set to 1
findings.summary: Argon2id parallelism parameter is set to 1, reducing GPU memory pressure for offline attackers.
findings.attackScenario: Same as PWD-001. Parallelism of 1 allows attackers to pack more hash candidates into GPU SRAM.
findings.impact: Marginal increase in offline cracking throughput relative to parallelism=4.
findings.rootCause: Defaulted to 1 without review of OWASP guidance.
findings.remediation: Addressed by PWD-001 remediation.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: parallelism is set to >= 4.
requiredTests: Same as PWD-001

findings.title: Pepper Not Enforced in Non-Production Environments
findings.summary: ARGON2_SECRET is optional in non-production environments. Staging environments may hash passwords without pepper protection.
findings.attackScenario: Staging environment accidentally classified as non-production (NODE_ENV not set to production). Passwords hashed without pepper. Breach of staging database exposes crackable hashes.
findings.impact: Staging/preview environments may have passwords stored without pepper protection.
findings.rootCause: Env schema marks ARGON2_SECRET as optional; boot guard only fails closed in production.
findings.remediation: Add check for NODE_ENV=staging or any non-development value to fail-closed. Document that staging environments MUST set NODE_ENV=production or ARGON2_SECRET.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Every non-development environment requires ARGON2_SECRET or logs a visible warning.
requiredTests: Boot app with NODE_ENV=test and no ARGON2_SECRET; verify warning or error emitted

findings.title: Login Timing Side-Channel Mitigation Delay Is Insufficient
findings.summary: Random delay max of 50ms does not adequately mask timing variance between real Argon2 verify and dummy verify. Statistical analysis of 1000+ samples can distinguish the two paths.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker measures response time differences between known email + wrong password (real verify ~50-200ms) and unknown email (dummy verify + 0-50ms delay). Collecting 1000+ samples statistically distinguishes the paths.
findings.impact: Account enumeration via timing analysis is possible, defeating the FIX-08 mitigation.
findings.rootCause: Random delay ceiling was chosen conservatively to avoid degrading UX but does not adequately mask timing variance.
findings.remediation: Increase random delay to cover full expected range of Argon2 verify times, or add fixed delay floor: FLOOR_MS=100 + JITTER_MS=100.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Timing distribution of unknown email responses is statistically indistinguishable from known email + wrong password under 1000+ samples (KS test p-value > 0.05).
requiredTests: Unit test: randomDelayMs(50) returns values in [0,50]
Integration test: Mock argon2.verify to fixed duration; verify total time matches
Load test: Measure timing distributions under simulated load

findings.title: Default Password Policy Has No Complexity Requirements
findings.summary: Default password policy does not require uppercase, lowercase, numbers, or special characters. Relies solely on zxcvbn strength scoring.
findings.attackScenario: User creates password like 'abcdefghijklmnop' (15 lowercase letters). Passes zxcvbn score check but lacks character class diversity.
findings.impact: Marginal reduction in password strength for users who create zxcvbn-acceptable but low-complexity passwords.
findings.rootCause: System deliberately relies on zxcvbn instead of prescriptive complexity rules (NIST 800-63B guidance).
findings.remediation: Enable requireUppercase:true and requireNumber:true in production policy, or raise zxcvbn threshold from score < 2 to score < 3.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Production password policy requires at least 2 character classes in addition to zxcvbn scoring.
requiredTests: Verify buildPasswordSchema with production policy rejects 'abcdefghijklmnop'
Verify accepts 'MyP@ssw0rd12345'
Verify zxcvbn blocks 'password123456789'

findings.title: Account Status Checks Leak Timing Information
findings.summary: Account status checks (suspended, deleted, disabled) are placed BEFORE password verification and do not run a dummy verify, leaking timing information.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker distinguishes between email not found (dummy verify + delay ~50-250ms) and email found but deleted/suspended (no verify, immediate throw <5ms).
findings.impact: Attacker can enumerate valid email addresses by measuring response times.
findings.rootCause: Status checks placed before password verification without timing mitigation.
findings.remediation: Move status checks after password verification, or run dummy verify + delay in status-check branches.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Timing distribution of 'email exists + deleted' and 'email does not exist' is statistically indistinguishable.
requiredTests: Unit test: Measure average response time for 'not found' vs 'deleted' paths; verify difference < 20ms

findings.title: Rate Limiting Collapses to Single Global Bucket Without Trusted Proxy
findings.summary: If TRUSTED_PROXY_IP_HEADER is not configured and boot guard is bypassed, all traffic resolves to 0.0.0.0 sentinel and shares one rate-limit bucket. 20 failed logins locks out ALL users platform-wide.
findings.attackScenario: Deployment skips env validation. All traffic resolves to 0.0.0.0 sentinel. Attacker makes 20 failed attempts, locking out all users for 15 minutes.
findings.impact: Availability DoS - all login attempts blocked for 15 minutes after ~20 failures from single attacker.
findings.rootCause: Fail-closed guard is correct but could potentially be bypassed by misconfigured deployment.
findings.remediation: Add runtime assertion in getClientIp() that sentinel is never used as rate-limit key.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Production deployment without TRUSTED_PROXY_IP_HEADER refuses to boot. Second defense-in-depth check prevents sentinel usage as rate-limit key.
requiredTests: Integration test: Boot with TRUSTED_PROXY_IP_HEADER unset in production; verify throw
Unit test: getClientIp() returns sentinel when no proxy header; verify rate-limit logs critical error

findings.title: Lockout Does Not Cap Maximum Lock Duration
findings.summary: Fixed 15-minute lockout duration without escalation. Attacker can keep account perpetually locked with 5 requests per 15 minutes.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker repeatedly triggers lockout: 5 failures -> 15 min lock -> 5 failures -> 15 min lock. Account permanently locked.
findings.impact: Targeted account denial-of-service. Only 5 requests per 15 minutes needed.
findings.rootCause: Lockout policy uses fixed duration without escalation or maximum total lock window.
findings.remediation: Implement escalating lockout durations (15 min, 30 min, 1 hour, 24 hours) or maximum total lock window with admin unlock mechanism.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: After 3 consecutive lockout cycles, lock duration escalates. Account auto-unlocked after maximum window or admin intervention.
requiredTests: Unit test: Simulate 3 lockout cycles; verify duration increases
Integration test: Verify account auto-unlocked after maximum window

findings.title: Math.random() Used for Timing Mitigation Delay
findings.summary: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure. Predictable delay values reduce effectiveness of timing normalization.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker observes enough delay values to predict PRNG state, subtracts predicted delay from total response time to recover Argon2 verify duration.
findings.impact: Marginal weakening of timing side-channel mitigation.
findings.rootCause: Math.random() used for non-security-critical delay without considering predictability.
findings.remediation: Replace with crypto.randomInt(max + 1) or modular reduction of crypto.randomBytes(4).
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Delay function uses cryptographically secure random source.
requiredTests: Unit test: randomDelayMs(50) returns values in [0,50]
Statistical test: Verify uniform distribution over 10,000 samples

findings.title: Password Change Action Derives Session ID from Client-Provided Cookie
findings.summary: Session ID derivation from client-provided cookie is correct but could be documented more clearly. Fail-safe behavior (revoke all sessions) is secure.
findings.attackScenario: N/A - the design is correct. If SESSION_SECRET is weak, getAuthSession() fails and currentSessionId is undefined, causing all sessions to be revoked (safe behavior).
findings.impact: Low. Session ID derivation is correct; fail-safe is secure.
findings.rootCause: N/A - design is correct but could be documented more clearly.
findings.remediation: Add comment explaining that currentSessionId is always derived server-side from getAuthSession() and never from client input.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Code comment documents the trust boundary. No functional change needed.
requiredTests: Existing tests for changePasswordAction cover both pending and authenticated flows

findings.title: Session Secret Minimum Length Is Adequate
findings.summary: 32-character hex string (128-bit entropy) is sufficient for HMAC-SHA256 session signing. No change needed.
findings.attackScenario: None - 128 bits of entropy is cryptographically secure for HMAC-SHA256.
findings.impact: None. Current configuration is secure.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed. Consider recommending openssl rand -hex 48 for defense-in-depth.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Session secret is >= 32 characters and not a known default.
requiredTests: Boot with session secret < 32 chars in production; verify refusal

findings.title: Reset Token Entropy Is 64 Bits Below NIST 128-Bit Minimum
findings.summary: Reset tokens use 8-byte (64-bit) entropy. NIST SP 800-63B requires minimum 128 bits for reset tokens.
findings.attackScenario: Offline brute-force of 16-char hex token. With rate limit of 10/15min, online brute-force infeasible. Risk is offline if token prefix exposed.
findings.impact: Token entropy below NIST minimum. Online brute-force infeasible due to rate limiting but offline risk exists if partial token exposed.
findings.rootCause: Default byteLength=8 chosen for URL brevity rather than NIST compliance.
findings.remediation: Increase default byteLength to 16 (128 bits, 32 hex chars) for password reset tokens.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Password reset tokens have >= 128 bits entropy (>= 16 random bytes). Token in email is >= 32 hex characters.
requiredTests: Verify generateToken(16) produces 32-character hex string
Verify reset email token is 32 hex characters
Statistical test: 10,000 tokens all unique with uniform distribution

findings.title: Reset Token Sent in URL Query String
findings.summary: Token embedded in URL query string may be logged in browser history, server logs, Referer headers, or proxy logs.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with access to browser history, server logs, or proxy logs uses token within 30-minute window.
findings.impact: Token exposure in logs/history, but mitigated by single-use + 30-min TTL + session revocation + confirmation email.
findings.rootCause: Standard pattern for email-based reset links (usability vs token exposure tradeoff).
findings.remediation: Add robots: noindex meta tag on reset page. Existing mitigations (single-use, TTL, session revocation, confirmation email) are sufficient.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Reset page includes robots: noindex. Token is single-use with 30-minute TTL.
requiredTests: Verify reset page includes meta robots noindex
Verify token cannot be reused after successful reset

findings.title: Reset Token Prefix Exposed in Rate-Limit Identifier
findings.summary: Rate-limit identifier uses raw token prefix. With 64-bit tokens (RST-001), prefix fully exposes token. After RST-001 fix, only half exposed.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with read access to login_attempts collection sees raw token prefix.
findings.impact: Low after RST-001 fix. Token prefix reveals only 64 of 128 bits.
findings.rootCause: Rate-limit identifier derived from raw token for simplicity.
findings.remediation: Hash token before using as rate-limit identifier after RST-001 fix.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Rate-limit identifier does not expose raw token.
requiredTests: Verify submitId does not contain raw token

findings.title: Reset Token Redemption Race Condition - Correctly Handled
findings.summary: TOCTOU gap exists but is safely handled by atomic findOneAndUpdate redemption. Code is correct.
findings.attackScenario: Concurrent requests with same token: both read, but atomic redeem ensures only one wins.
findings.impact: None. TOCTOU gap is safely handled.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding demonstrating correct concurrent-safety design.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Redeem operation is atomic; only one concurrent request succeeds.
requiredTests: Fire 10 concurrent reset requests with same token; verify exactly one succeeds

findings.title: Reset Rate Limiting Split Across Two Layers with Different Identifiers
findings.summary: Action and service layers use different rate-limit identifier formats, meaning they do not share counters.
findings.attackScenario: An attacker could potentially bypass one layer if the other has a bug.
findings.impact: Low - both layers use same 5-request/15-minute window but different identifier formats.
findings.rootCause: Action layer added later as pre-flight throttle with different identifier format.
findings.remediation: Unify identifier format between layers or remove service-layer throttle.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Layers share same rate-limit counter or one layer is removed.
requiredTests: Make 5 reset requests; verify 6th throttled by action layer
Verify service-layer throttle also reached if action-layer bypassed

findings.title: Reset Completion Rate Limit Uses Raw Token Prefix
findings.summary: Rate-limit identifier for reset completion derived from first 16 characters of raw token.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker observes identifier from login_attempts collection, recovers token prefix.
findings.impact: Low - after RST-001 fix (32-char tokens), only half token exposed.
findings.rootCause: Using raw token prefix simpler than hashing for rate-limit key.
findings.remediation: Hash token before using as rate-limit identifier.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: submitId does not contain any portion of raw token.
requiredTests: Verify submitId does not match any prefix of raw token
Verify rate limiting still works with hashed identifier

findings.title: Reset Link Uses APP_URL - Host Header Poisoning Mitigated
findings.summary: Reset link constructed from APP_URL server-side env var, not from request Host header. Host header poisoning not possible.
findings.attackScenario: None - link uses APP_URL, not Host header.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Reset link always uses APP_URL.
requiredTests: Send request with forged Host header; verify reset link still uses APP_URL

findings.title: All Sessions Revoked on Password Reset
findings.summary: All sessions revoked on password reset including current session. Correct behavior to prevent session fixation.
findings.attackScenario: None - all sessions properly invalidated after reset.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: All sessions revoked after password reset.
requiredTests: Create 3 sessions; perform reset; verify all 3 revoked

findings.title: Pending Reset Tokens Invalidated on Password Change
findings.summary: Pending reset tokens correctly invalidated when password is changed through normal flow.
findings.attackScenario: User requests reset then changes password. Pending token invalidated.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Pending reset tokens invalidated when password is changed.
requiredTests: Request reset; change password via settings; verify token no longer valid

findings.title: Password Change Requires Current Password
findings.summary: Password change requires current password verification. Prevents attacker with stolen session from changing password.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with stolen session tries to change password to maintain access. Blocked by current password requirement.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Password change rejects requests without valid current password.
requiredTests: Attempt password change with wrong current password; verify rejection
Attempt with correct; verify success

findings.title: Password Change Revokes All Other Sessions
findings.summary: Password change correctly revokes all other sessions except current. Prevents session fixation.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker changes password. All other sessions revoked, preventing session fixation.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: All sessions except current revoked on password change.
requiredTests: Create 3 sessions; change password from session 1; verify sessions 2 and 3 revoked

findings.title: Password Change Confirmation Email Sent After Reset
findings.summary: Confirmation email sent to user after successful password reset. Alerts legitimate user of unauthorized changes.
findings.attackScenario: None - email notifies legitimate user.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Confirmation email sent after successful reset.
requiredTests: Perform reset; verify confirmation email sent
Verify email contains contact-admin message

findings.title: Force-Change Path Issues Signed Pending Cookie
findings.summary: cws_pw_pending cookie is HMAC-signed with SESSION_SECRET and carries userId. Low risk due to HMAC protection, short TTL, and SameSite=Strict.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker forges pending cookie (requires weak SESSION_SECRET). Could impersonate user and force password change.
findings.impact: Low - cookie is HMAC-signed, short-lived (10 min), SameSite=Strict, Secure, HttpOnly.
findings.rootCause: Pending cookie is a signed bearer token. Security depends on SESSION_SECRET strength.
findings.remediation: Existing controls sufficient. Consider adding HttpOnly flag if not already set.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, 10-minute max-age.
requiredTests: Verify cookie options include httpOnly, secure, sameSite strict
Verify cookie cleared after successful password change

findings.title: No Clock Skew Leeway for id_token Expiry
findings.summary: Token expiry uses strict comparison with no leeway. Legitimate users experience intermittent login failures due to network latency or clock skew.
findings.attackScenario: Network latency or clock skew causes token exp to be slightly in past by verification time.
findings.impact: Legitimate users experience intermittent login failures. Not exploitable for security bypass.
findings.rootCause: claims.exp < now uses strict comparison. Google recommends accepting tokens up to 5 minutes before/after expiry.
findings.remediation: Add 5-minute (300 second) leeway: claims.exp + 300 < now. Consider making configurable via env.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Token with exp up to 5 minutes in past is accepted; > 5 minutes past is rejected.
requiredTests: Token with exp = now - 299 passes verification
Token with exp = now - 301 fails verification

findings.title: State Comparison Not Constant-Time
findings.summary: State comparison uses JavaScript string inequality instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual. Practical exploitation extremely unlikely for 256-bit random state.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker performs timing side-channel analysis on state comparison to gradually learn state value.
findings.impact: Extremely unlikely given 256-bit entropy, JS string equality properties, and per-IP rate limit.
findings.rootCause: Uses state !== expectedState instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual.
findings.remediation: Convert both strings to Buffers and use crypto.timingSafeEqual.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: State comparison uses crypto.timingSafeEqual; timing consistency confirmed.
requiredTests: Verify state comparison returns false for single-character mismatch with consistent timing

findings.title: Web Path Does Not Check email_verified
findings.summary: Web OAuth path does not check email_verified while mobile path does. Inconsistency is a defense-in-depth concern.
findings.attackScenario: Google issues id_token with email_verified: false. Web path accepts if sub matches pre-provisioned row.
findings.impact: Low in practice (pre-provisioned accounts verified by admin), but inconsistency between web and mobile paths.
findings.rootCause: handleCallbackInternal does not check profile.email_verified. Mobile path does.
findings.remediation: Add email_verified check in handleCallbackInternal, mirroring mobile path.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Both web and mobile OAuth paths reject tokens with email_verified: false.
requiredTests: Test handleCallbackInternal with email_verified: false and verify rejection

findings.title: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI Not Conditionally Required
findings.summary: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI is optional even when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is set. Runtime failure instead of boot-time detection.
findings.attackScenario: Operator sets GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID but forgets GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI. App boots but Google login fails at runtime.
findings.impact: Misconfiguration leads to non-functional Google login with confusing runtime error.
findings.rootCause: validateSecurityConfig checks GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET but not GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI.
findings.remediation: Add GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI to conditional requirement check when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is set.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Boot fails in production when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID set without GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI.
requiredTests: Boot with GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID set and GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI absent; verify expected error

findings.title: JWKS Fetch Does Not Validate Key Types
findings.summary: JWKS cache accepts any key with kid,n,e without filtering by kty: RSA or use: sig.
findings.attackScenario: Google JWKS includes non-RSA keys. Cache stores them but createPublicKey fails. RS256 check prevents misuse.
findings.impact: None in practice - Google uses RSA, RS256 check prevents confusion.
findings.rootCause: JwksCacheEntry type accepts any key without filtering by kty.
findings.remediation: Filter JWKS keys to kty: RSA and use: sig when populating cache.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Non-RSA keys silently ignored; only RSA signing keys cached.
requiredTests: Test with JWKS containing mixed key types; verify only RSA used

findings.title: Per-IP Rate Limit Shared Across All Users
findings.summary: Per-IP rate limit shared across all users. Behind NAT or VPN, attacker shares IP with legitimate users.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker behind NAT exhausts 20/15min IP limit, blocking legitimate users on same IP.
findings.impact: DoS for legitimate users sharing attacker's IP. 20/15min is generous for OAuth flows.
findings.rootCause: Rate limiting keyed by IP only, not IP + user.
findings.remediation: Consider per-user rate limiting alongside per-IP. Accept current design with documentation.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Rate limiting design documented; 20/15min appropriate for deployment.
requiredTests: Document rate limiting design decision

findings.title: Mobile Path Skips Nonce Verification
findings.summary: Mobile path accepts id_token directly without nonce binding. Standard pattern for mobile OIDC.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker replays captured mobile id_token. Mitigated by token short lifetime, sub matching, risk evaluation.
findings.impact: None - standard mobile OIDC pattern with token short lifetime and pre-provisioning.
findings.rootCause: Mobile clients do not use authorization code flow with nonce.
findings.remediation: Acceptable as-is for mobile pattern. Document that mobile relies on token short lifetime.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Mobile path rejects expired, malformed, wrong-issuer/audience tokens.
requiredTests: Verify mobile path rejects expired tokens
Verify audience validation

findings.title: No iat Claim Validation
findings.summary: iat (issued-at) claim not validated. Token could be replayed for up to 1 hour (Google's default id_token lifetime).
findings.attackScenario: Attacker obtains valid unexpired Google id_token and replays it.
findings.impact: Limited by exp claim (1 hour max). Web path state cookie prevents replay. Mobile path relies on exp.
findings.rootCause: iat claim not validated. While not strictly required by OIDC Core, max-age would reduce replay window.
findings.remediation: Add iat validation with configurable maximum age as defense-in-depth.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Tokens with iat older than configured max age rejected.
requiredTests: Test with valid token where iat beyond max age

findings.title: State Cookie Contains All Secrets in Single JSON Blob
findings.summary: State, PKCE code verifier, and nonce in single JSON blob. Cookie properties (httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax) provide sufficient protection.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with XSS reads httpOnly cookie. If attacker has XSS, they can already steal session cookies.
findings.impact: None - httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax, 10-minute maxAge.
findings.rootCause: All three secrets serialized in one cookie.
findings.remediation: Acceptable as-is. Splitting would not materially improve security.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Cookie has correct properties.
requiredTests: Verify cookie properties: httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax, maxAge 600

findings.title: OAuth Callback Error Logs Internal Messages
findings.summary: Internal error messages logged server-side. Client-facing redirects use generic error codes.
findings.attackScenario: Internal error messages accessible via log aggregation misconfiguration.
findings.impact: Information disclosure to log aggregators. Client-side messages are generic.
findings.rootCause: console.error logs full error object.
findings.remediation: Ensure log aggregation has proper access controls.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: OAuth errors logged server-side; client redirects use generic error codes.
requiredTests: Verify client receives generic error codes, not internal messages

findings.title: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET Not Required in Non-Production
findings.summary: Non-production environments warn but don't fail for missing GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET. Production correctly enforces.
findings.attackScenario: Dev environment boots with warning; Google login fails at runtime.
findings.impact: Runtime failure only in non-production. Production boot guard correct.
findings.rootCause: Dev path warns but does not fail.
findings.remediation: Acceptable design. Dev permissive, production enforced.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Production boot fails without GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID set.
requiredTests: Verify production boot fails without secret when ID set

findings.title: prompt: select_account Prevents Account Chooser Bypass
findings.summary: prompt: select_account ensures user must always select Google account, preventing session fixation or account chooser bypass.
findings.attackScenario: None - positive control preventing forced authentication with specific account.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Account chooser always shown.
requiredTests: Verify prompt parameter set in authorization URL

findings.title: alertingService Failures Are Swallowed
findings.summary: Alerting service failures silently dropped. OAuth abuse patterns may go undetected. Audit log provides backup record.
findings.attackScenario: Alerting service unavailable. OAuth failures not alerted.
findings.impact: Reduced visibility into attack patterns. Audit log is backup.
findings.rootCause: Alerting failures caught and logged but not propagated.
findings.remediation: Acceptable for resilience. Ensure audit log provides sufficient forensic data.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: OAuth failures always recorded in audit log.
requiredTests: Verify audit log entries created for OAuth failures

findings.title: providerEmail Not Normalized on Storage
findings.summary: providerEmail stored without normalization. Could cause false mismatches in future features.
findings.attackScenario: Google provides email with non-standard casing. Future comparison with internal email fails.
findings.impact: Low - providerEmail not used for access control. Could cause confusion in future UI.
findings.rootCause: providerEmail stored directly from Google profile without normalization.
findings.remediation: Apply trim().toLowerCase() before storage in link().
findings.acceptanceCriteria: providerEmail always stored normalized.
requiredTests: Test link() with mixed-case email; verify stored value is lowercase

findings.title: No Unique Index Enforcement on (provider, providerAccountId)
findings.summary: No unique index on (provider, providerAccountId). Concurrent link() calls could create duplicate entries.
findings.attackScenario: Two concurrent requests call link() with same (provider, providerAccountId) but different userId. Both insert, creating duplicate link.
findings.impact: Latent vulnerability exploitable when public linking API is added. Current link() only callable server-side.
findings.rootCause: link() uses find-then-insert without unique index guarantee.
findings.remediation: Add unique compound index on { provider: 1, providerAccountId: 1 }. Handle duplicate key errors idempotently.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: MongoDB has unique index; concurrent link() calls produce exactly one document.
requiredTests: Concurrent insertion test; verify exactly one document exists after both complete

findings.title: No Database-Level Uniqueness for (userId, provider)
findings.summary: Multiple Google links could exist per user. No unique index on (userId, provider).
findings.attackScenario: link() called multiple times for same (userId, provider) with different providerAccountId creates duplicates.
findings.impact: Login still works (findByProvider looks by sub), but could cause confusion in account management.
findings.rootCause: No unique index on (userId, provider).
findings.remediation: Document intended policy (one Google per user). Add appropriate unique indexes.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Linking policy documented; appropriate unique indexes exist.
requiredTests: Test linking second Google account to same user; verify update or rejection

findings.title: No Audit Trail for OAuth Account Linking Events
findings.summary: No audit log entry when admin links Google account. Forensic capability reduced.
findings.attackScenario: Admin links account but no audit record. Incident investigation impossible.
findings.impact: Reduced forensic capability. linkedAt records creation time but not who created it.
findings.rootCause: link() does not emit audit log entries.
findings.remediation: Log auth.oauth.linked audit event when linking UI/API is added.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Every oauth_accounts CRUD operation logged with actor identity.
requiredTests: Verify audit log entries created for linking operations

findings.title: No Mechanism to Revoke Google OAuth Refresh Tokens
findings.summary: No mechanism to revoke Google-side refresh tokens. Application does not store Google refresh tokens.
findings.attackScenario: Compromised Google account continues to authenticate. App has no way to revoke Google tokens.
findings.impact: Low - app only uses id_token, no refresh tokens stored. Revocation must be done via Google Account settings.
findings.rootCause: OAuth flow only exchanges code for id_token; no refresh token requested or stored.
findings.remediation: Document that Google account revocation must be done via Google Account settings.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Documentation covers Google-side revocation; no Google refresh tokens stored.
requiredTests: Verify documentation covers Google-side revocation

findings.title: Pre-Provisioned Link to Active User Check - Positive
findings.summary: Login correctly checks user.status !== active even when pre-provisioned link exists.
findings.attackScenario: Admin provisions link for user then deactivates user. Login correctly rejected.
findings.impact: None - positive control working correctly.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: Consider cleanup job for oauth_accounts rows for deleted users.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Login rejected when linked user inactive.
requiredTests: Verify login rejected for inactive linked user

findings.title: link() Method Does Not Validate User Existence
findings.summary: link() creates oauth_accounts row without verifying target userId exists in users collection.
findings.attackScenario: Admin calls link() with non-existent userId. Orphaned oauth_accounts row created.
findings.impact: Data integrity issue. Login would fail at userId lookup anyway.
findings.rootCause: link() inserts directly without verifying target userId existence.
findings.remediation: Add pre-check in link() or rely on login-time check and accept orphaned rows.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: link() either validates user existence or documents that it does not.
requiredTests: Test link() with non-existent userId; verify behavior

findings.title: OTP Token Type Filter Not Passed to redeem()
findings.summary: redeem() in TwoFactorService.verify() does not filter by type. Cross-type reuse is cryptographically infeasible but lacks defense-in-depth.
findings.attackScenario: Theoretically, password_reset token with same SHA-256 hash could be redeemed by OTP path. In practice cryptographically infeasible.
findings.impact: Informational - SHA-256 collision resistance makes cross-type reuse infeasible.
findings.rootCause: redeem() called without type filter.
findings.remediation: Pass type: 'two_factor' to redeem() for defense-in-depth.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: redeem() filters by token type.
requiredTests: Verify OTP verification only redeems two_factor type tokens

findings.title: Code-Sent Audit Logs Missing IP Address
findings.summary: Code-sent audit event logs ipAddress: null because sendCode() called before session exists.
findings.attackScenario: Code-sent audit event lacks IP for forensic analysis.
findings.impact: Incomplete audit trail for code-sent events.
findings.rootCause: sendCode() called before session creation; IP not available.
findings.remediation: Pass IP from caller through sendCode(userId, {ipAddress, userAgent}).
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Code-sent audit event includes IP and user-agent.
requiredTests: Verify code-sent audit log includes IP and user-agent

findings.title: TOTP Secrets Stored in Plaintext
findings.summary: TOTP secrets stored as plaintext Base32 in MongoDB. DB compromise exposes all TOTP secrets for indefinite code generation.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with DB read access (leak, backup, injection) extracts all TOTP secrets. Generates valid codes indefinitely.
findings.impact: Complete 2FA bypass for all TOTP-enrolled users. Attacker generates valid tokens indefinitely.
findings.rootCause: Secret stored without application-layer encryption.
findings.remediation: Encrypt TOTP secret at application layer (AES-256-GCM) or use MongoDB CSFLE.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: TOTP secrets unreadable without encryption key; verifyTotpLogin decrypts before verification.
requiredTests: Verify verifyTotpLogin works with encrypted secrets
Verify DB dump does not reveal plaintext secrets

findings.title: QR Code otpauth:// URL Returned in Server Action Response
findings.summary: otpauth:// URL containing plaintext secret returned in Server Action response. Server Actions use POST so not cached by default.
findings.attackScenario: Response cached by CDN, proxy, or browser extension. Secret exposed.
findings.impact: Low - Server Actions use POST, not cached by default. Browser bfcache may hold temporarily.
findings.rootCause: URL returned in Server Action response rather than one-time-use endpoint.
findings.remediation: Consider one-time-use endpoint for otpauth:// URL, or advise client to clear after QR generation.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: otpauth:// URL not cached in shared caches.
requiredTests: Verify Server Action response has no-cache headers

findings.title: TOTP Verification Has No Per-User Rate Limit
findings.summary: No independent per-user TOTP verification rate limit. Only protected by PendingAuthentication.attemptsRemaining (5 per login transaction).
findings.attackScenario: Attacker obtains multiple valid pending auth tokens. Each allows 5 TOTP guesses. 5*N total attempts across N sessions.
findings.impact: Elevated brute-force surface across parallel login sessions.
findings.rootCause: No cross-session aggregate per-user TOTP failure limit.
findings.remediation: Add per-user TOTP failure rate limit (e.g., 5 failures per 15 minutes).
findings.acceptanceCriteria: After N failed TOTP attempts within time window, further attempts rejected regardless of pending auth tokens.
requiredTests: Verify per-user aggregate failure counter blocks beyond threshold

findings.title: No TOTP-Specific Lockout
findings.summary: Unlike email OTP which invalidates code after 5 failures, TOTP path has no equivalent lockout. TOTP secret remains active regardless of failures.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker brute-forces TOTP codes without triggering any TOTP-specific lockout.
findings.impact: TOTP secret remains active regardless of failed attempts.
findings.rootCause: No per-user TOTP failure counter like email OTP's MAX_2FA_FAILURES.
findings.remediation: Implement per-user TOTP failure counter (5 per 15 min) mirroring email OTP behavior.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: After 5 consecutive TOTP failures within 15 min, user temporarily blocked from TOTP verification.
requiredTests: Verify TOTP verification blocked after 5 failures within 15 min

findings.title: Server Clock Synchronization Informational
findings.summary: Standard cloud NTP configuration. Tolerance of +/-1 time step (30 seconds) via otplib default. No clock drift detection.
findings.attackScenario: Server clock drift outside tolerance window.
findings.impact: Informational - cloud platforms maintain accurate time.
findings.rootCause: N/A - standard practice.
findings.remediation: Consider logging server time difference on TOTP verification for operational visibility.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: TOTP verification works with standard cloud NTP.
requiredTests: Verify TOTP verification succeeds within tolerance window

findings.title: 2FA Can Be Disabled Without Reauthentication
findings.summary: disableTotpAction only requires requireActiveSession(), not password or TOTP re-entry. Attacker with stolen session can disable TOTP.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker steals session cookie from trusted device. Calls disableTotpAction. TOTP disabled without re-proving identity.
findings.impact: Complete 2FA removal without re-proving identity. Future logins skip MFA.
findings.rootCause: disableTotpAction only requires session validity, not reauthentication.
findings.remediation: Require password re-entry or valid TOTP code before disabling TOTP.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: disableTotpAction rejects request if user cannot prove current password or TOTP possession.
requiredTests: Verify disable fails without password
Verify disable succeeds with correct password

findings.title: TOTP Replacement Without Confirming Existing Factor
findings.summary: User can generate new TOTP secret without verifying existing TOTP. saveTotpSecret() silently replaces via upsert.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with valid session generates new TOTP secret, sets up in own authenticator, verifies new code. Victim's TOTP replaced.
findings.impact: Attacker gains control of second factor. Victim's legitimate authenticator no longer works.
findings.rootCause: No check for existing TOTP status or requirement to verify current TOTP before replacement.
findings.remediation: When user has totpEnabled: true, require current TOTP verification before generating new secret.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: If user.security.totpEnabled === true, TOTP replacement requires current TOTP verification.
requiredTests: Verify new enrollment works when no TOTP exists
Verify replacement requires current TOTP verification

findings.title: Trusted Devices Never Expire
findings.summary: trustedUntil always set to null. Devices remain trusted indefinitely with no maximum trust duration.
findings.attackScenario: User trusts device at conference. Device later lost or sold. Remains trusted indefinitely.
findings.impact: Attacker with physical access to trusted device can skip MFA on future logins.
findings.rootCause: No expiry logic; trustedUntil always null.
findings.remediation: Set trustedUntil to reasonable expiry (e.g., 90 days). Check expiry in 2FA step-up decision.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Trusted devices automatically untrust after configured duration.
requiredTests: Verify device untrusted after configured duration
Verify MFA required after trust expiry

findings.title: No Explicit Session Rotation After 2FA Completion
findings.summary: After 2FA verification, new session is created via createSession(). Functionally equivalent to session rotation.
findings.attackScenario: Session fixation via pre-2FA session reuse.
findings.impact: None - new session created; pending cookie consumed and cleared.
findings.rootCause: N/A - security goal achieved through different mechanism.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: New session created after 2FA; pending cookie cleared.
requiredTests: Verify new session after 2FA; verify pending cookie cleared

findings.title: Session ID is MongoDB ObjectId (96-bit entropy)
findings.summary: Session IDs are MongoDB ObjectIds (96 bits) signed with HMAC-SHA256. Sufficient entropy with forgery prevention.
findings.attackScenario: None - 96 bits sufficient against brute-force; HMAC prevents forgery.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Session IDs have sufficient entropy and HMAC signing.
requiredTests: Verify session cookie contains HMAC-signed ObjectId

findings.title: Session Cookie Flags Correctly Configured
findings.summary: Session cookie uses HttpOnly, Secure (production), SameSite Lax. Refresh cookie uses SameSite Strict with scoped path.
findings.attackScenario: None - all cookie security flags correctly configured.
findings.impact: None. Excellent defense-in-depth.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Cookie flags correctly set.
requiredTests: Verify cookie flags in production HTTP responses

findings.title: Logout Revokes Session and Refresh Family
findings.summary: Logout revokes both session and refresh token family, then clears browser cookies. Comprehensive logout.
findings.attackScenario: None - logout is comprehensive.
findings.impact: None. Positive finding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Logout revokes session, refresh tokens, and clears cookies.
requiredTests: Verify session and refresh revoked on logout

findings.title: Atomic Refresh Token Rotation Prevents Replay
findings.summary: Atomic findOneAndUpdate ensures only one concurrent rotation wins. Loser routed to reuse-revoke path. Textbook refresh token rotation.
findings.attackScenario: Stolen refresh token used concurrently. Atomic replacement ensures only one wins; reuse triggers revocation.
findings.impact: None. Excellent implementation.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Atomic refresh rotation prevents concurrent replay.
requiredTests: Verify concurrent refresh attempts: one succeeds, one triggers revocation

findings.title: Device Binding on Refresh Tokens
findings.summary: Refresh tokens bound to device record. Mismatch treated as theft, triggering session revocation and alerting.
findings.attackScenario: Stolen refresh token used on different device. Device mismatch triggers revocation.
findings.impact: None. Excellent device binding.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Refresh tokens bound to device; mismatch triggers revocation.
requiredTests: Verify refresh rejected when device mismatch
Verify alert on mismatch

findings.title: EdDSA JWT with Explicit Algorithm Allowlist
findings.summary: Mobile JWT uses EdDSA (Ed25519) with explicit algorithm allowlist. Prevents algorithm confusion attacks.
findings.attackScenario: None - algorithm is hardcoded and explicitly allowlisted.
findings.impact: None. Excellent implementation.
findings.rootCause: N/A - positive finding.
findings.remediation: No change needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: JWT uses EdDSA with explicit allowlist.
requiredTests: Verify JWT verification rejects non-EdDSA tokens

findings.title: Mobile Admin Routes Missing Bearer Authentication
findings.summary: Mobile admin routes for categories, products, and session revocation lack authenticateBearerRequest(). Rely on cookie-based requireActiveSession() which fails for mobile clients.
findings.attackscenario: Mobile app sends bearer token; receives 500 because requireActiveSession() cannot read bearer token.
findings.impact: Functional regression - mobile clients cannot use these endpoints. No authorization bypass.
findings.rootCause: Inconsistent application of authenticateBearerRequest() across mobile admin routes.
findings.remediation: Add authenticateBearerRequest() or authenticateCookieOrBearer() to affected routes.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Every /api/mobile/v1/admin/* route calls authenticateBearerRequest() or authenticateCookieOrBearer().
requiredTests: Test each mobile admin endpoint with valid bearer token, valid session cookie, no credentials, invalid token

findings.title: revokeSessionAction Trusts User-Supplied currentSessionId
findings.summary: revokeSessionActionImpl takes currentSessionId from form data instead of verifying caller's session. Ownership check passes because both sessions belong to same user.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker invokes Server Action with different currentSessionId than their actual session. Both belong to same user, ownership check passes.
findings.impact: Potential horizontal privilege escalation for session revocation. Low practical risk due to encrypted action IDs and high-entropy session IDs.
findings.rootCause: revokeSessionActionImpl does not call requireActiveSession(). Trusts form-supplied currentSessionId.
findings.remediation: Add requireActiveSession() and use authenticated session for ownership verification.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Caller must be authenticated; ownership check uses authenticated session, not user input.
requiredTests: Authenticated user cannot revoke another user's sessions
Unauthenticated invocation rejected
Different currentSessionId than actual session is rejected

findings.title: Health Endpoint Publicly Accessible
findings.summary: GET /api/health exposes database health status without authentication. Standard for health checks but reveals infrastructure status.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker determines if MongoDB is reachable.
findings.impact: Minor information disclosure of infrastructure status.
findings.rootCause: Health endpoint designed for load balancers/monitors without auth.
findings.remediation: Consider restricting to internal networks or adding API key for production.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Endpoint returns 200 with healthy status or 503 with error.
requiredTests: Verify health endpoint returns 200 or 503 appropriately

findings.title: Test Cookies Endpoint Left in Codebase
findings.summary: GET /api/auth/test-cookies sets test cookie and redirects. Development utility not removed from codebase.
findings.attackScenario: Endpoint accessible in production. Sets inert test cookie.
findings.impact: Minimal - only sets test_cookie and redirects. No auth impact.
findings.rootCause: Development utility not removed before deployment.
findings.remediation: Remove from production builds or gate behind NODE_ENV=development.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Route not accessible in production.
requiredTests: Verify route returns 404 in production

findings.title: Category and Product CRUD Actions Missing withCsrfGuard
findings.summary: CMS CRUD actions are 'use server' but not wrapped with withCsrfGuard. Reduced CSRF defense depth per project convention.
findings.attackScenario: Malicious website creates form that POSTs to these actions. Protected by Next.js action IDs and server-side auth, but explicit origin check missing.
findings.impact: Reduced CSRF defense depth. Still protected by: Next.js action IDs, requireCmsPermission(), HttpOnly cookies.
findings.rootCause: Actions added before withCsrfGuard convention established.
findings.remediation: Wrap all exported functions with withCsrfGuard.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: All 'use server' data-modifying actions wrapped with withCsrfGuard.
requiredTests: Verify cross-origin requests to these actions rejected

findings.title: Debug File Writes in verify-2fa.ts
findings.summary: fs.appendFileSync writes debug info to debug-verify.log on every 2FA verification. Creates filesystem write and unbounded log growth.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with filesystem access reads device IDs and trust status. Unbounded disk growth.
findings.impact: Information disclosure; operational concern (disk space, no log rotation).
findings.rootCause: Debugging code left in codebase.
findings.remediation: Remove fs.appendFileSync calls. Use structured logging through audit log repository.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: No appendFileSync calls in production code paths.
requiredTests: Verify no filesystem writes outside established logging

findings.title: CSP Only Applied to Dashboard Routes
findings.summary: CSP header only applied to /dashboard/* routes. Public site routes do not receive CSP headers.
findings.attackScenario: Public site without CSP may be vulnerable to XSS if user content rendered.
findings.impact: Acceptable if public site doesn't handle user-generated content. Should be reviewed.
findings.rootCause: Public site may have different CSP requirements.
findings.remediation: Review public site for user content rendering; add CSP if needed.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Public site CSP reviewed; applied if user content rendered.
requiredTests: Verify CSP header present on dashboard routes

findings.title: Contact Form Endpoint Lacks CSRF Protection
findings.summary: POST /api/contact is public endpoint with no CSRF protection. Could be used for spam.
findings.attackScenario: Malicious website auto-submits contact form for spam.
findings.impact: Potential spam. No auth or data breach risk.
findings.rootCause: Public endpoint without CSRF protection.
findings.remediation: Add assertSameOriginStrict() or rate limiting per IP.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Cross-origin submissions rejected.
requiredTests: Verify cross-origin POST to /api/contact rejected

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Session Refresh Endpoint
findings.summary: No per-IP rate limit on POST /api/auth/refresh. Flooding could exhaust MongoDB connection pool on shared Atlas.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker floods refresh endpoint. Each call triggers MongoDB read+write. Exhausts connection pool (maxPoolSize: 10).
findings.impact: DoS against all authenticated users; database connection pool exhaustion.
findings.rootCause: Relies on origin check and token rotation; no explicit rate limit.
findings.remediation: Add per-IP rate limit (60/min) using existing LoginAttemptRepository pattern.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/refresh enforces per-IP rate limit. Exceeding returns 429 with Retry-After.
requiredTests: Verify 429 returned when per-IP refresh limit exceeded

findings.title: TOTP Verification Has No Dedicated IP-Based Rate Limit
findings.summary: No per-user aggregate TOTP failure rate limit. Multiple pending sessions allow 5*N total TOTP attempts.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker generates multiple pending sessions. Each allows 5 TOTP guesses. No cross-session aggregate limit.
findings.impact: Elevated brute-force surface on TOTP codes across parallel sessions.
findings.rootCause: Only attemptsRemaining checked per pending auth, not cross-session aggregate.
findings.remediation: Add per-user TOTP failure rate limit (10 per 15 min) using LoginAttemptRepository.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Per-user aggregate failure counter checked before TOTP verification.
requiredTests: Verify block when per-user aggregate failures exceed limit

findings.title: Recovery Code Brute-Force Shares 2FA Failure Window
findings.summary: Recovery codes and email 2FA codes share same 5-per-15min failure counter. Attacker alternates between methods within budget.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker submits recovery codes and email codes interchangeably. Both consume same MAX_2FA_FAILURES counter.
findings.impact: 5-per-15-min aggregate limit applies but attacker gets two verification methods.
findings.rootCause: countRecent2FAFailures counter shared between email and recovery code failures.
findings.remediation: Separate per-user counter for recovery code failures (e.g., 3 per 15 min).
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Recovery code failures tracked with dedicated counter.
requiredTests: Verify recovery code attempts blocked after dedicated failure limit

findings.title: Per-IP Login Rate Limit Collapses to Global Bucket Without Trusted Proxy
findings.summary: Without TRUSTED_PROXY_IP_HEADER (prevented by boot guard), all traffic resolves to 0.0.0.0 sentinel. 20 cross-user failures lock out all logins.
findings.attackScenario: If boot guard bypassed, all traffic into one bucket. ~20 failures lock out all users.
findings.impact: Platform-wide login lockout. Mitigated by boot guard.
findings.rootCause: Trusted-proxy header mandatory in production; sentinel guard skips IP limits.
findings.remediation: Already mitigated. Boot guard prevents this. Sentinel guard in rate-limit.service.ts provides defense-in-depth.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Production boot fails without TRUSTED_PROXY_IP_HEADER.
requiredTests: Verify boot fails without header in production

findings.title: IPv6 Address Normalization Not Enforced for Rate Limiting
findings.summary: IPv6 addresses not normalized. Different textual representations create separate rate-limit buckets.
findings.attackScenario: IPv6 client sends requests using different address representations. Each creates separate bucket.
findings.impact: Per-IP rate limits bypassed for IPv6 clients.
findings.rootCause: getClientIp() returns raw header value without IPv6 normalization.
findings.remediation: Normalize IPv6 addresses in getClientIp().
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Equivalent IPv6 representations produce same rate-limit bucket key.
requiredTests: Verify equivalent IPv6 representations normalized to same value

findings.title: No Global IP Lockout Across Accounts
findings.summary: Attacker rotates through known emails from same IP. Each gets separate per-email counters. Per-IP limit (20/15min) partially mitigates.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker tries 20 different emails from same IP within 15 min.
findings.impact: Credential enumeration across multiple accounts.
findings.rootCause: Lockout per-user; per-IP limit is only cross-account throttle.
findings.remediation: Consider more aggressive per-IP failure limit or escalating IP lockout.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Per-IP failure count limits total cross-account attempts.
requiredTests: Verify block when per-IP failures exceed limit across accounts

findings.title: Password Reset Request Allows Repeated Cycles
findings.summary: No daily cap on password reset requests. Attacker can email-bomb target with up to 480 emails per 24 hours.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker requests reset, waits 15 min, requests again. 5 per 15-min window = 480 per 24 hours.
findings.impact: Email bombing / harassment of target user.
findings.rootCause: Sliding 15-min window with no daily cap.
findings.remediation: Add daily cap (e.g., 15 per 24 hours) using MongoDB-backed counter.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Per-email daily limit enforced.
requiredTests: Verify block after daily limit reached

findings.title: Serverless Race Condition on Rate-Limit Counters
findings.summary: Rate-limit check uses countDocuments + separate insertOne (non-atomic). Concurrent requests may exceed intended limit by 1-3.
findings.attackScenario: Two concurrent requests both read count below threshold, both proceed.
findings.impact: Rate limits slightly exceeded under high concurrency. Acceptable for current scale.
findings.rootCause: Read-then-write pattern, not atomic. MongoDB doesn't provide compare-and-swap on count.
findings.remediation: For exact enforcement, use $inc-based counter. Document accepted race window.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Race window documented; limit effective against sequential attacks.
requiredTests: Verify slight over-count under concurrent inserts but block sequential attacks

findings.title: Login Failure Spike Alerting Uses In-Memory Aggregation
findings.summary: Spike detection uses in-memory Map. In serverless, each instance has independent buckets. Distributed attack diluted across instances.
findings.attackScenario: Distributed brute-force spreads failures across instances. No single instance sees threshold.
findings.impact: Spike detection unreliable in serverless.
findings.rootCause: In-memory aggregation not shared across processes.
findings.remediation: Increase spike threshold for serverless or move to MongoDB-backed counter.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Spike detection works in single-instance; multi-instance limitation documented.
requiredTests: Verify spike alert triggers in single-instance mode

findings.title: No Rate Limiting for WebAuthn Endpoints
findings.summary: WebAuthn login-options endpoint lacks IP-based rate limiting. Could be abused for high database write volume.
findings.attackScenario: Attacker floods login-options to trigger expensive challenge generation.
findings.impact: Database write amplification; compute cost increase.
findings.rootCause: WebAuthn endpoints lack explicit rate limiting.
findings.remediation: Add per-IP rate limit (20 per 15 min) on login-options endpoint.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/webauthn/login-options enforces per-IP rate limit.
requiredTests: Verify rate limit on WebAuthn login-options by IP

findings.title: HSTS Must Be Configured at the Edge
findings.summary: HSTS must be configured at the edge platform (Vercel/Netlify). Without it, first HTTP requests send session cookies in cleartext.
findings.attackScenario: User navigates to admin dashboard over HTTP. SSL stripping attack intercepts session cookie before redirect to HTTPS.

findings.acceptanceCriteria: E2E test verifies Strict-Transport-Security with max-age >= 31536000. Deployment docs specify edge header config.
requiredTests: E2E test: verify HSTS header present on admin routes
E2E test: verify max-age >= 31536000

requiredTests: Verify error does not contain password from MONGODB_URI

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy Directives for Modern Browser Features

findings.title: Debug File Writes Left in Production 2FA Code Path

findings.title: Database Config Error Leaks Partial Connection String
findings.summary: Database config error includes first 20 characters of MONGODB_URI, potentially exposing username and password prefix.

findings.impact: Partial credential leakage in error messages.

findings.acceptanceCriteria: Error message includes at most scheme portion, not authority.
requiredTests: Verify error message does not contain password

findings.title: Security Webhook Is Optional and Falls Back to Console
findings.summary: Without SECURITY_WEBHOOK_URL, all critical security events emitted as console.warn. May be lost in serverless environments.
findings.attackScenario: Critical events (token reuse, failure spikes) lost in serverless stdout capture.
findings.impact: Critical security events undetected. Incident response delayed.
findings.rootCause: Webhook sink is opt-in. No startup warning or boot guard.
findings.remediation: Add startup warning when SECURITY_WEBHOOK_URL unset in production. Consider hard requirement.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Startup warning emitted when SECURITY_WEBHOOK_URL unset in production.
requiredTests: Verify warning when SECURITY_WEBHOOK_URL unset in production

findings.title: login_attempts TTL Is Only 24 Hours
findings.summary: login_attempts TTL is 24 hours. After 24 hours, all records auto-deleted. Forensic evidence lost for incidents discovered after window.
findings.attackScenario: Slow brute-force campaign discovered after 24 hours. Evidence unavailable.
findings.impact: Loss of forensic evidence for incidents discovered after 24 hours.
findings.rootCause: TTL set for storage efficiency conflicting with forensic needs.
findings.remediation: Extend TTL to at least 7 days (604,800 seconds). Consider 30-90 days for compliance.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: login_attempts TTL is at least 7 days.
requiredTests: Verify TTL index >= 604800 seconds

findings.title: No Automated Dependency Vulnerability Scanning
findings.summary: No pnpm audit in CI pipeline. Known vulnerabilities in dependencies persist until manually discovered.
findings.attackScenario: Dependency publishes known vulnerability. Without automated scanning, persists indefinitely.
findings.impact: Known vulnerabilities remain unpatched; potential exploitation.
findings.rootCause: Build pipeline has custom source-code scanner but not dependency scanner.
findings.remediation: Add pnpm audit to CI. Enable Dependabot or Renovate. Add test:security script.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: pnpm audit runs in CI on every PR. Critical vulnerabilities block deployment.
requiredTests: CI workflow runs pnpm audit --audit-level=critical

findings.title: In-Memory Failure Spike Buckets Reset on Process Restart
findings.summary: In-memory failureBuckets map resets on each new serverless instance. Distributed brute-force never reaches spike threshold.
findings.attackScenario: Distributed attack across instances never triggers spike alert.
findings.impact: Spike detection unreliable in serverless.
findings.rootCause: In-memory aggregation not shared across processes.
findings.remediation: Move spike detection to MongoDB or accept as known limitation.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Limitation documented; single-instance detection verified.
requiredTests: Verify spike alert triggers in single-instance mode

findings.title: Audit Log Retention Is 180 Days
findings.summary: Audit log retention is 180 days. SOC 2 Type II recommends 1 year.
findings.attackScenario: Compliance gap if SOC 2 required.
findings.impact: May not meet SOC 2 retention requirements.
findings.rootCause: TTL set to 180 days for storage efficiency.
findings.remediation: Verify 180 days meets compliance. Extend to 365 days if SOC 2 required.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Retention meets organizational compliance requirements.
requiredTests: Verify TTL >= 15552000 seconds

findings.title: Mail Delivery Failures Silently Swallowed
findings.summary: Mail delivery failures caught and logged but not forwarded to alerting service. Users cannot complete 2FA or reset without visible error.
findings.attackScenario: Gmail SMTP issues cause silent delivery failures. Users stuck at 2FA step.
findings.impact: Users cannot complete authentication without visible error or alert.
findings.rootCause: Mailer catches errors but doesn't forward to alerting sink.
findings.remediation: Forward mail failures to alerting sink. Consider circuit breaker pattern.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Mail failures forwarded to security alerting sink.
requiredTests: Verify mail failures trigger alerting event

findings.title: No Startup Banner or Version Identification
findings.summary: No startup log with environment info. Slows incident response when identifying running version and features.
findings.attackScenario: Incident response delayed while identifying running version.
findings.impact: Slower incident response; difficulty correlating logs across environments.
findings.rootCause: getEnv() validates and caches but does not log environment info.
findings.remediation: Add structured startup log with NODE_ENV, APP_URL, enabled features, version.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Structured startup log emitted; contains no secret values.
requiredTests: Verify startup banner with APP_URL, features, version
